title: Bengaluru to Goa Road Trip: Routes via Hubballi and the Ghats
seoTitle: Bengaluru to Goa Road Trip: Via Hubballi and the Ghats | Kudozz Club
metaDescription: Bengaluru to Goa by road: NH48 via Chitradurga and Hubballi, then Belagavi and Chorla ghat or the Anmod route, with detours to Hampi, Dandeli and Gokarna.
description: A route guide to the Bengaluru to Goa road trip: NH48 via Tumakuru, Chitradurga, Davanagere and Hubballi–Dharwad, then into Goa via Belagavi and the Chorla ghat or via Ramnagar and the Anmod ghat, or down to the coast at Karwar, with approximate distance and time, detours to Hampi, Dandeli, Jog Falls and Gokarna, and seasons.
dek: Bengaluru to Goa is a long but easy highway drive across the Deccan, finishing with a descent through the Western Ghats.

hero.alt: The road through Chorla Ghat on the Karnataka–Goa border

intro: Most drivers go from Bengaluru to Goa on NH48, the Mumbai highway, through Tumakuru, Chitradurga, Davanagere and Hubballi–Dharwad. From there, the choice is how to cross the Western Ghats: via Belagavi and the Chorla ghat into north Goa, via Ramnagar and the Anmod ghat towards Ponda and south Goa, or west to Karwar and along the coast. The Deccan stretch is fast and flat; the ghats are slower and forested.
With detours to Hampi, Dandeli or Gokarna, the drive becomes a satisfying three- to five-day trip.
quickAnswer: Bengaluru to Goa is about 560 to 600 km and usually takes 10 to 11 hours via NH48 to Hubballi–Dharwad, then through the Western Ghats via Belagavi and Chorla, or via the Anmod ghat. Good detours include Chitradurga fort, Hampi, Dandeli and Gokarna via the coast. October to March is best; the ghat sections can be slow in the monsoon, and the Anmod route has seen repair closures.
takeaways: NH48 to Hubballi is a fast four- and six-lane highway.
Choose your ghat: Chorla via Belagavi, Anmod via Ramnagar, or the coast via Karwar.
Check the status of the Anmod ghat, which has had repair closures.
Hampi, Dandeli and Gokarna turn the drive into a multi-day trip.
Fuel and food are easy on NH48; ghat sections have fewer services.

sections.heading: Crossing the Western Ghats
paras: The Chorla ghat links Belagavi with north Goa through forest and is popular in the monsoon for its mist and waterfalls. The Anmod ghat on NH748 has had periods of repair and restrictions on heavy vehicles; check its status before choosing it. The Karwar route adds the coast and is the natural choice if you want Gokarna.

sections.heading: Driving considerations
list: Leave Bengaluru early to clear the city before Tumakuru.
NH48 carries heavy trucks; keep a safe distance and avoid tired late-night driving.
Ghat roads are narrow; give way to uphill traffic and avoid overtaking on bends.
Goa's roads are narrow and busy with scooters; drive slowly in villages.

sections.heading: Food along the way
paras: Davanagere is famous for benne dosa, and Hubballi–Dharwad for Dharwad pedha. In Goa, fish thali, xacuti and bebinca await at the end of the drive.

sections.heading: When to go
paras: October to March is best, with dry roads and pleasant Goa weather. The monsoon (June to September) makes the ghats beautiful but slippery, with occasional landslides and fog. Hampi is hot from April to June.

safety: On ghat roads, use low gears downhill, give way to uphill traffic where the road is narrow, and do not overtake on blind bends.
Mountain roads close or slow down after heavy rain, snow or landslides; check road status and weather updates each morning and avoid driving after dark.
Permits, tolls, entry fees, pass openings and road works change; check official sources shortly before you travel.
Distances and driving times are approximate and vary with traffic, weather, road works and stops.
packing: Driving licence, RC, insurance and PUC certificate, with copies
Warm layers and a rain jacket
Cash for small towns and barriers

faqs.q: How far is Goa from Bengaluru by road?
faqs.a: About 560 to 600 km, depending on the route.

faqs.q: How long does the drive take?
faqs.a: Usually 10 to 11 hours without long stops.

faqs.q: Which ghat is best into Goa from Bengaluru?
faqs.a: Chorla via Belagavi is the most common; check the Anmod ghat's status before using it.

faqs.q: Can I visit Hampi on the way to Goa?
faqs.a: Yes; it is a detour of a few hours and worth a night.

faqs.q: Is the Bengaluru–Goa drive good in the monsoon?
faqs.a: The ghats are beautiful but slower and slippery; drive in daylight.

faqs.q: Can I drive along the coast from Karwar to Goa?
faqs.a: Yes; the coastal route via Karwar suits a stop at Gokarna.
